Rapitest Soil Test Kit 1601, pH comparator

The pH procedure on manual page 1 uses the green comparator, soil fill line, one matching green powder capsule, preferably distilled water to its fill line, a tight cap, shaking, about one minute for settling/colour development, and that comparator's own chart in daylight away from direct sun. These instructions are not interchangeable with the NPK tests or another kit.

Before practical scoring, the trainer records the actual kit make/model, current manual revision, reagent SDS and chart range; the learner follows those exact instructions. If these are unavailable, only the simulation can proceed and no practical pass is awarded.
Check sample identity, matched chart, label/SDS and PPE
Soil to this comparator’s soil line
One matching green pH capsule
Water to this comparator’s water line
Fit the cap and shake thoroughly
Allow settling and colour development: about 1 minute for this example
Compare liquid above soil with its own chart in diffuse daylight
Record supported result and clean/dispose by site procedure

units.delivery: Explain calmly and naturally to agricultural vocational learners in clear English. Read only the supplied connected passage with natural pauses. Preserve all negations, conditions, scene-safety restrictions and limits of training. Do not add medical advice, diagnoses, character voices, an introduction, music or an extra summary.

sourceBindings.text: Trainer records the exact kit and manual and directly observes each learner use the correct sample fill/measure, matched pH reagent quantity, specified water and closure, mixing and real development wait; no substituted time or amount from another kit.

Pass only when every kit-specific stage is correctly performed by that learner with compatible PPE. If the physical kit/manual/SDS is missing, record unassessed and allow online rehearsal without practical credit.

Trainer observes same-kit chart comparison in diffuse daylight, identifies the actual sample, verifies value or interval is within chart scale, and records uncertainty or poor colour match instead of invented decimal precision.
Pass when identity, chart, supported reading and recording are all correct. A universal blue/purple rule, a borrowed chart or an out-of-range guess does not pass.

Trainer observes safe PPE, bench hygiene, correct cleaning and site-specific waste separation and hears a comparison of quick field-kit screening with calibrated meter/lab testing and its limitations.
Pass only with both observed safe completion and a justified method choice. Unsupervised reagent use or unsafe disposal is a stop-and-remediate condition.

sourceBindings.text: The eight checks are correct sample amount, reagent quantity, water fill, capped shaking for the actual kit’s duration, settling/colour development, comparison with the matching chart, recording the value, and cleaning the equipment/bench. Also record PPE and SDS checks, chart identity and uncertainty. Use the actual manufacturer’s values; do not invent them.

Retain source's PPE, correct soil/reagent/water, manufacturer mixing/development, chart reading and cleanup/disposal checks. Only an individually observed learner under the actual kit protocol can pass.

Trainer selects the actual kit, verifies manual/SDS and pretests samples A/B/C. Each learner measures under observation, records actual result and uncertainty, cleans and disposes safely. Group recorder/analyst roles rotate, but one learner's test does not pass another.
